typeset.css

The CSS implementation. Everything is scoped to .typeset, so it cannot leak into surrounding markup. Drop it in and add the class.

Fonts are not included. The page must load EB Garamond, Source Sans 3 and IBM Plex Mono itself. For a document you send, self-host and embed them rather than fetching from a CDN at print time — and note that Google's build of EB Garamond has no real small caps, so the browser synthesises them. Browse the font files →

1/* ==========================================================================
2 typeset.css — a print stylesheet for essays, letters, and reports.
3 Units are in points. Everything is scoped to `.typeset`.
4 ========================================================================== */
5
6/*! @s tokens :: Tokens */
7.typeset {
8 /* Families */
9 --ts-serif: "EB Garamond", "Iowan Old Style", Palatino, Georgia, serif;
10 --ts-sans: "Source Sans 3", "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
11 --ts-mono: "IBM Plex Mono", "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
12
13 /* Scale — 11pt base, ~1.2 ratio */
14 --ts-xs: 8pt;
15 --ts-sm: 9.5pt;
16 --ts-base: 11pt;
17 --ts-h4: 12pt;
18 --ts-h3: 14pt;
19 --ts-h2: 18pt;
20 --ts-h1: 24pt;
21
22 /* Rhythm */
23 --ts-leading: 1.45;
24 --ts-leading-tight: 1.2;
25 --ts-space: 11pt; /* one line of base leading, near enough */
26 --ts-measure: 33em; /* ~66 characters at 11pt serif */
27
28 /* Ink — never pure black: it blooms on laser and glares in a PDF */
29 --ts-ink: #1a1a1a;
30 --ts-ink-muted: #5a5a5a;
31 --ts-ink-faint: #8a8a8a;
32 --ts-rule: #c9c4bd;
33 --ts-rule-strong: #6f6a64;
34 --ts-wash: #f4f1ec;
35 --ts-accent: #7a1f1f; /* oxblood: reads as dark grey in greyscale */
36}
37/*! @e */
38
39/*! @s foundation :: Foundation */
40.typeset {
41 font-family: var(--ts-serif);
42 font-size: var(--ts-base);
43 font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums proportional-nums;
44 line-height: var(--ts-leading);
45 color: var(--ts-ink);
46 text-rendering: optimizeLegibility;
47 font-kerning: normal;
48 font-feature-settings: "liga" 1, "kern" 1;
49}
50
51/* Measure is a property of the text column, not the page. */
52.typeset > * {
53 max-width: var(--ts-measure);
54}
55
56.typeset--measure-wide { --ts-measure: 40em; }
57.typeset--measure-narrow { --ts-measure: 27em; }
58/*! @e */
59
60/*! @s page :: Page setup */
61/* Symmetric is what a document gets unless it asks for binding: the named
62 size applies to all four sides. `standard` is the default size, set here on
63 the unqualified page — every named page below is a page-name override of
64 just its margins, and everything else on this rule (size, running head,
65 folio, first-page suppression) still cascades onto it. */
66@page {
67 size: A4; /* or: Letter */
68 margin: 20mm; /* foundation.page.margins.symmetric_mm.standard */
69
70 /* Margin boxes need a paged-media engine: Paged.js, WeasyPrint, Prince.
71 Chrome's own print dialog ignores them. */
72 @top-center {
73 content: string(ts-running-head);
74 font: 8pt/1 "Source Sans 3", sans-serif;
75 letter-spacing: 0.08em;
76 text-transform: uppercase;
77 color: #8a8a8a;
78 }
79 @bottom-center {
80 content: counter(page);
81 font: 9pt/1 "EB Garamond", serif;
82 font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums;
83 color: #5a5a5a;
84 }
85}
86
87/* No running head or folio on the opening page. */
88@page :first {
89 @top-center { content: none; }
90 @bottom-center { content: none; }
91}
92
93/* The running head follows the current section. */
94.typeset h2 { string-set: ts-running-head content(text); }
95
96/* The three symmetric sizes, the same value on every side. `standard` names
97 the default set above; the class exists so a document can ask for it back
98 explicitly, the same as narrow and wide. */
99.typeset--margin-narrow { page: ts-margin-narrow; }
100.typeset--margin-standard { page: ts-margin-standard; }
101.typeset--margin-wide { page: ts-margin-wide; }
102
103@page ts-margin-narrow { margin: 10mm; }
104@page ts-margin-standard { margin: 20mm; }
105@page ts-margin-wide { margin: 30mm; }
106
107/* Duplex: the explicit opt-in for a sheet that will be bound. Top and bottom
108 stay at the symmetric value; left and right split into an inner (binding)
109 edge and an outer edge, mirrored by page side so the gutter stays on the
110 spine rather than swapping sides every other sheet. */
111.typeset--margin-duplex-narrow { page: ts-margin-duplex-narrow; }
112.typeset--margin-duplex-standard { page: ts-margin-duplex-standard; }
113.typeset--margin-duplex-wide { page: ts-margin-duplex-wide; }
114
115@page ts-margin-duplex-narrow { margin-top: 10mm; margin-bottom: 10mm; }
116@page ts-margin-duplex-narrow:right { margin-left: 13mm; margin-right: 7mm; }
117@page ts-margin-duplex-narrow:left { margin-left: 7mm; margin-right: 13mm; }
118
119@page ts-margin-duplex-standard { margin-top: 20mm; margin-bottom: 20mm; }
120@page ts-margin-duplex-standard:right { margin-left: 23mm; margin-right: 17mm; }
121@page ts-margin-duplex-standard:left { margin-left: 17mm; margin-right: 23mm; }
122
123@page ts-margin-duplex-wide { margin-top: 30mm; margin-bottom: 30mm; }
124@page ts-margin-duplex-wide:right { margin-left: 33mm; margin-right: 27mm; }
125@page ts-margin-duplex-wide:left { margin-left: 27mm; margin-right: 33mm; }
126/*! @e */
127
128/*! @s headings :: Headings */
129/* The shared base every heading level builds on: line-height, color, margin rhythm and break behaviour. Not a style in its own right — each level below overrides family, weight and size to become itself. */
130.typeset h1,
131.typeset h2,
132.typeset h3,
133.typeset h4,
134.typeset h5,
135.typeset h6 {
136 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
137 font-weight: 600;
138 line-height: var(--ts-leading-tight);
139 color: var(--ts-ink);
140
141 /* A heading belongs to what follows it, not to what precedes it. */
142 margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 2) 0 calc(var(--ts-space) * 0.5);
143
144 /* Never strand a heading at the foot of a page. */
145 break-after: avoid;
146 break-inside: avoid;
147 text-wrap: balance;
148}
149
150/* @style headings-h1 */
151.typeset h1 {
152 font-size: var(--ts-h1);
153 font-weight: 300;
154 letter-spacing: -0.015em;
155 margin-top: 0;
156}
157
158/* @style headings-h2 */
159.typeset h2 {
160 font-size: var(--ts-h2);
161 letter-spacing: -0.01em;
162}
163
164/* @style headings-h3 */
165.typeset h3 { font-size: var(--ts-h3); }
166
167/* @style headings-h4 */
168.typeset h4 { font-size: var(--ts-h4); }
169
170/* Below h4, drop the size change and shift register instead. */
171/* @style headings-h5 */
172.typeset h5 {
173 font-size: var(--ts-base);
174 font-family: var(--ts-serif);
175 font-weight: 600;
176 font-variant-caps: all-small-caps;
177 letter-spacing: 0.06em;
178}
179
180/* @style headings-h6 */
181.typeset h6 {
182 font-size: var(--ts-base);
183 font-family: var(--ts-serif);
184 font-weight: 400;
185 font-style: italic;
186}
187
188/* A run-in heading: the h6 sits on the first line of its paragraph. */
189.typeset .ts-headings-run-in {
190 display: inline;
191 margin: 0;
192}
193.typeset .ts-headings-run-in + p { display: inline; }
194.typeset .ts-headings-run-in::after { content: " · "; color: var(--ts-ink-faint); }
195/*! @e */
196
197/*! @s numbering :: Section numbering */
198.typeset--numbered { counter-reset: ts-headings-h2; }
199
200/* @style numbering-h2 */
201.typeset--numbered h2 {
202 counter-increment: ts-headings-h2;
203 counter-reset: ts-headings-h3;
204}
205.typeset--numbered h2::before {
206 content: counter(ts-headings-h2) " ";
207 color: var(--ts-ink-faint);
208 font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums;
209}
210
211/* @style numbering-h3 */
212.typeset--numbered h3 { counter-increment: ts-headings-h3; }
213.typeset--numbered h3::before {
214 content: counter(ts-headings-h2) "." counter(ts-headings-h3) " ";
215 color: var(--ts-ink-faint);
216 font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums;
217}
218/*! @e */
219
220/*! @s paragraphs :: Paragraphs */
221/* @style paragraphs-spaced */
222.typeset {
223 /* Paragraph separation is one decision expressed as two values: a gap, or an
224 indent, never both. A template sets these; nothing else needs to know. */
225 --ts-para-gap: var(--ts-space);
226 --ts-para-indent: 0;
227}
228
229/* @style paragraphs-indented */
230.typeset--indented {
231 --ts-para-gap: 0;
232 --ts-para-indent: 1.5em;
233}
234
235.typeset p {
236 margin: 0 0 var(--ts-para-gap);
237 text-indent: var(--ts-para-indent);
238 orphans: 2; /* no single line left at the foot of a page */
239 widows: 2; /* no single line carried to the head of the next */
240}
241
242/* The first paragraph after a heading, block or break is flush: the thing above
243 it has already marked the start.
244
245 Enumerated rather than written as `:is(...)`. Paged.js rewrites every
246 stylesheet through its own CSS parser, which does not understand `:is()`: it
247 splits the selector on the commas INSIDE the argument list and emits
248 fragments like ` .ts-callouts-callout)+p`, which throw on querySelectorAll
249 and abort pagination entirely — a blank document, not a degraded one. Keep
250 this list flat. */
251.typeset h1 + p,
252.typeset h2 + p,
253.typeset h3 + p,
254.typeset h4 + p,
255.typeset h5 + p,
256.typeset h6 + p,
257.typeset blockquote + p,
258.typeset figure + p,
259.typeset pre + p,
260.typeset table + p,
261.typeset hr + p,
262.typeset .ts-break + p,
263.typeset .ts-callouts-callout + p,
264.typeset > p:first-child {
265 text-indent: 0;
266}
267/*! @e */
268
269/*! @s justification :: Justification & hyphenation */
270/* Justification without hyphenation opens rivers of white space.
271 Both, or neither. And `lang` must be set — hyphenation is per-language. */
272/* @style justification-justified */
273.typeset--justified {
274 text-align: justify;
275 text-align-last: left; /* the last line is never stretched */
276 text-justify: inter-word;
277 hyphens: auto;
278 hyphenate-limit-chars: 6 3 3; /* min word, before break, after break */
279 -webkit-hyphenate-limit-before: 3;
280 -webkit-hyphenate-limit-after: 3;
281 hyphenate-limit-lines: 2; /* never stack 3 hyphens in a row */
282}
283
284/* Ragged right. This is the default — the point of naming it is so a document
285 can state the choice rather than express it as the absence of a class, and so
286 the two options read as siblings in the source.
287
288 `text-wrap: pretty` asks the engine to spend more effort on the rag: it
289 avoids a very short last line and evens out the right edge, which is the one
290 thing a ragged setting can get wrong. Hyphenation stays off — a hyphen exists
291 to help justification, and without justification it only breaks a word for
292 no gain. */
293/* @style justification-ragged */
294.typeset--ragged {
295 text-align: left;
296 text-align-last: left;
297 hyphens: manual;
298 text-wrap: pretty;
299}
300
301/* `text-align-last` inherits as well, so a block that centres itself must
302 restore it — otherwise its last line, which for a one-line block is its only
303 line, is flushed left. See .ts-quotes-pullquote and .ts-break.
304
305 Never justify a heading, a cell, or a listing. Every other block that must
306 stay flush left — subtitle, byline, caption, address, notes — declares
307 `text-align: left` in its own rule, because a direct match always beats an
308 inherited value and its descendants then inherit `left` in turn. Relying on
309 an exception list here instead means every new block silently opts in. */
310/* @style justification-exclusions — headings h1-h4, body cells and listings are pulled back to flush under .typeset--justified; every other never-justified block declares text-align: left in its own rule, per the note above. */
311.typeset--justified h1,
312.typeset--justified h2,
313.typeset--justified h3,
314.typeset--justified h4,
315.typeset--justified td,
316.typeset--justified pre { text-align: left; hyphens: manual; }
317/*! @e */
318
319/*! @s dropcap :: Drop cap */
320.typeset .ts-dropcap::first-letter {
321 float: left;
322 font-family: var(--ts-serif);
323 font-size: 3.05em; /* tuned to cover exactly three lines */
324 line-height: 0.86;
325 font-weight: 400;
326 color: var(--ts-accent);
327 padding: 0.02em 0.06em 0 0;
328}
329.typeset .ts-dropcap { text-indent: 0; }
330
331/* A drop cap wants the opening words in small caps to bridge the size jump. */
332.typeset .ts-dropcap-lede { font-variant-caps: all-small-caps; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
333/*! @e */
334
335/*! @s inline :: Inline emphasis */
336/* @style inline-strong */
337.typeset strong, .typeset b { font-weight: 600; }
338/* @style inline-emphasis */
339.typeset em, .typeset i { font-style: italic; }
340/* @style inline-emphasis-nested */
341.typeset em em, .typeset em i { font-style: normal; } /* nested emphasis flips */
342.typeset strong em, .typeset em strong { font-weight: 600; font-style: italic; }
343
344/* Small caps for named entities, acronyms, and stage directions. */
345.typeset .ts-inline-small-caps {
346 font-variant-caps: all-small-caps;
347 letter-spacing: 0.05em;
348 font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums;
349}
350
351/* @style inline-abbr */
352.typeset abbr[title] {
353 font-variant-caps: all-small-caps;
354 letter-spacing: 0.05em;
355 text-decoration: none;
356 border-bottom: 0.5pt dotted var(--ts-ink-faint);
357}
358
359/* @style inline-deleted */
360.typeset s, .typeset del { text-decoration: line-through; color: var(--ts-ink-muted); }
361/* @style inline-inserted */
362.typeset ins { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 0.15em; }
363/* @style inline-highlight */
364.typeset mark { background: var(--ts-wash); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2pt var(--ts-wash); }
365
366/* Real super/subscripts, not shifted full-size digits. */
367/* @style inline-superscript */
368/* @style inline-subscript */
369.typeset sup, .typeset sub {
370 font-size: 0.72em;
371 line-height: 0;
372 position: relative;
373 vertical-align: baseline;
374}
375.typeset sup { top: -0.45em; }
376.typeset sub { bottom: -0.22em; }
377
378/* @style inline-kbd */
379.typeset kbd {
380 font: 0.85em/1 var(--ts-sans);
381 padding: 0.15em 0.35em;
382 border: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
383 border-bottom-width: 1.5pt;
384 border-radius: 2pt;
385}
386/*! @e */
387
388/*! @s code-inline :: Inline code */
389/* @style code-inline */
390.typeset code {
391 font-family: var(--ts-mono);
392 font-size: 0.86em; /* mono runs large; pull it back optically */
393 font-variant-ligatures: none;
394 background: var(--ts-wash);
395 padding: 0.1em 0.28em;
396 border-radius: 2pt;
397 overflow-wrap: break-word;
398}
399/*! @e */
400
401/*! @s links :: Links in print */
402/* @style links-link */
403.typeset a {
404 color: inherit;
405 text-decoration: underline;
406 text-decoration-thickness: 0.5pt;
407 text-underline-offset: 0.14em;
408 text-decoration-skip-ink: auto;
409}
410
411/* Paper has no hover. Spell out external URLs where they carry information. */
412@media print {
413 /* @style links-print-url */
414 .typeset a[href^="http"]::after {
415 content: " (" attr(href) ")";
416 font: 0.82em var(--ts-mono);
417 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
418 word-break: break-all;
419 }
420 /* Internal and mailto links read fine as-is. */
421 .typeset a[href^="#"]::after,
422 .typeset a[href^="mailto"]::after,
423 .typeset a.ts-links-bare::after { content: none; }
424}
425/*! @e */
426
427/*! @s numerals :: Numerals */
428/* Old-style figures sit in the x-height and belong in running prose.
429 Lining figures are uniform-height and belong in headings and tables.
430 Tabular figures share one advance width so columns align. */
431.typeset .ts-numerals-prose { font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums proportional-nums; }
432.typeset .ts-numerals-display { font-variant-numeric: lining-nums proportional-nums; }
433.typeset .ts-numerals-tabular { font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums; }
434.typeset .ts-numerals-fractions { font-variant-numeric: diagonal-fractions; }
435/*! @e */
436
437/*! @s quotes :: Block quotations */
438/* @style quotes-blockquote */
439.typeset blockquote {
440 margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.25) 0;
441 padding-left: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5);
442 border-left: 1pt solid var(--ts-rule);
443 color: var(--ts-ink);
444 font-size: 10.5pt;
445 break-inside: avoid;
446}
447.typeset blockquote > :last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }
448
449/* Attribution: an em dash, and never inside the quote. */
450.typeset blockquote cite,
451.typeset .ts-quotes-attribution {
452 display: block;
453 text-align: left;
454 margin-top: calc(var(--ts-space) * 0.5);
455 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
456 font-style: normal;
457 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
458}
459.typeset blockquote cite::before,
460.typeset .ts-quotes-attribution::before { content: "— "; }
461
462/* An epigraph opens a chapter: no rule, indented from the right, italic. */
463.typeset .ts-quotes-epigraph {
464 border: 0;
465 text-align: left;
466 margin: 0 0 calc(var(--ts-space) * 2) auto;
467 padding: 0;
468 max-width: 24em;
469 font-style: italic;
470 font-size: 10pt;
471 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
472}
473.typeset .ts-quotes-epigraph cite { font-style: normal; }
474
475/* A pull quote is display type lifted from the body. It repeats — so it must
476 never be the only place a claim appears. */
477.typeset .ts-quotes-pullquote {
478 border: 0;
479 text-align: center;
480 text-align-last: center;
481 border-top: 1.5pt solid var(--ts-rule-strong);
482 border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
483 padding: var(--ts-space) 0;
484 margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5) 0;
485 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
486 font-size: 15pt;
487 font-weight: 300;
488 line-height: 1.3;
489 text-wrap: balance;
490}
491
492/* Verse: preserve the poet's line breaks, indent the runovers. */
493.typeset .ts-quotes-verse {
494 border: 0;
495 text-align: left;
496 padding-left: calc(var(--ts-space) * 2);
497 white-space: pre-line;
498 font-size: var(--ts-base);
499 text-indent: -1.5em;
500 padding-inline-start: calc(var(--ts-space) * 2 + 1.5em);
501}
502/*! @e */
503
504/*! @s lists :: Lists */
505.typeset ul,
506.typeset ol {
507 margin: 0 0 var(--ts-space);
508 padding-left: 1.4em;
509}
510.typeset li { margin-bottom: calc(var(--ts-space) * 0.25); }
511.typeset li > ul,
512.typeset li > ol { margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 0.25) 0 0; }
513.typeset li:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }
514
515/* @style lists-unordered */
516.typeset ul { list-style: none; }
517.typeset ul > li::before {
518 content: "·";
519 float: left;
520 width: 1.4em;
521 margin-left: -1.4em;
522 text-align: left;
523 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
524 font-weight: 700;
525}
526/* @style lists-unordered-nested */
527.typeset ul ul > li::before { content: "–"; font-weight: 400; }
528
529/* @style lists-ordered */
530.typeset ol {
531 list-style: none;
532 counter-reset: ts-ol;
533}
534.typeset ol > li { counter-increment: ts-ol; }
535.typeset ol > li::before {
536 content: counter(ts-ol) ".";
537 float: left;
538 width: 1.4em;
539 margin-left: -1.4em;
540 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
541 font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums;
542}
543/* @style lists-ordered-nested */
544.typeset ol ol > li::before { content: counter(ts-ol, lower-alpha) "."; }
545
546/* A tight list for enumerations that are not prose. */
547.typeset .ts-lists-tight li { margin-bottom: 0; }
548
549/* Definition lists: the right shape for terms, glossaries, and letter fields. */
550.typeset dl { margin: 0 0 var(--ts-space); }
551/* @style lists-definition-term */
552.typeset dt {
553 text-align: left;
554 font-weight: 600;
555 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
556 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
557 margin-top: calc(var(--ts-space) * 0.6);
558 break-after: avoid;
559}
560.typeset dt:first-child { margin-top: 0; }
561/* @style lists-definition-description */
562.typeset dd { margin: 0 0 0 calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5); }
563/*! @e */
564
565/*! @s tables :: Tables */
566/* @style tables-table */
567.typeset table {
568 width: 100%;
569 border-collapse: collapse;
570 margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.25) 0;
571 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
572 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
573 font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums;
574 line-height: 1.35;
575}
576
577/* Rules, not grids. Vertical rules are almost never needed — the columns
578 already read as columns. */
579/* @style tables-cell */
580.typeset th,
581.typeset td {
582 padding: 0.45em 0.7em 0.45em 0;
583 text-align: left;
584 vertical-align: baseline;
585 border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
586}
587.typeset th:last-child,
588.typeset td:last-child { padding-right: 0; }
589
590/* @style tables-header-cell */
591.typeset thead th {
592 font-weight: 600;
593 font-size: var(--ts-xs);
594 letter-spacing: 0.07em;
595 text-transform: uppercase;
596 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
597 border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ts-rule-strong);
598}
599.typeset tbody tr:last-child td { border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ts-rule-strong); }
600/* @style tables-footer-cell */
601.typeset tfoot td { font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 0; }
602
603/* Numbers align on their right edge. Units go in the header, not every cell. */
604.typeset .ts-tables-cell-numeric { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums; }
605.typeset th.ts-tables-cell-numeric { text-align: right; }
606
607/* Repeat the header on every page a long table spans. */
608.typeset thead { display: table-header-group; }
609.typeset tfoot { display: table-footer-group; }
610/* @style tables-row */
611.typeset tr { break-inside: avoid; }
612
613/* @style tables-caption */
614.typeset caption {
615 caption-side: top;
616 text-align: left;
617 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
618 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
619 color: var(--ts-ink);
620 padding-bottom: 0.5em;
621 max-width: none;
622}
623/* The shared base under every caption/label variant: small-caps, weight and
624 tracking common to a table caption's label, a figure caption's label, the
625 abstract's label and a letter address block's label. Not a style in its
626 own right — always written alongside one of the four named classes below,
627 which each carry what makes their label different from the others. */
628.typeset .ts-label {
629 font-weight: 600;
630 font-variant-caps: all-small-caps;
631 letter-spacing: 0.06em;
632}
633/* Empty on purpose: the base above already carries everything a table
634 caption's label needs. The class exists so the style has a name. */
635.typeset .ts-tables-caption-label { }
636
637/* Optional zebra for wide, dense tables only. */
638.typeset .ts-tables-zebra tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: var(--ts-wash); }
639/*! @e */
640
641/*! @s codeblock :: Code blocks */
642/* @style codeblock */
643.typeset pre {
644 font-family: var(--ts-mono);
645 font-size: 8.5pt;
646 line-height: 1.45;
647 background: var(--ts-wash);
648 border-left: 2pt solid var(--ts-rule-strong);
649 padding: 0.8em 1em;
650 margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.25) 0;
651 overflow-x: auto;
652
653 /* Paper cannot scroll. Wrap, and mark the wrap. */
654 white-space: pre-wrap;
655 overflow-wrap: break-word;
656 tab-size: 2;
657 break-inside: avoid;
658}
659.typeset pre code {
660 background: none;
661 padding: 0;
662 font-size: inherit;
663}
664
665@media print {
666 .typeset pre { break-inside: auto; } /* long listings must be allowed to split */
667}
668/*! @e */
669
670/*! @s figures :: Figures & captions */
671/* @style figures-figure */
672.typeset figure {
673 margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5) 0;
674 break-inside: avoid;
675}
676.typeset figure img,
677.typeset figure svg {
678 display: block;
679 max-width: 100%;
680 height: auto;
681}
682/* @style figures-caption */
683.typeset figcaption {
684 text-align: left;
685 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
686 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
687 line-height: 1.4;
688 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
689 margin-top: 0.5em;
690 padding-top: 0.4em;
691 border-top: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
692}
693.typeset .ts-figures-caption-label { color: var(--ts-ink); }
694/*! @e */
695
696/*! @s notes :: Footnotes & endnotes */
697/* The reference mark. Superscript, no brackets, and it must not disturb
698 the line's leading. */
699.typeset .ts-notes-marker {
700 font-size: 0.7em;
701 line-height: 0;
702 position: relative;
703 top: -0.45em;
704 font-variant-numeric: lining-nums;
705 text-decoration: none;
706 color: var(--ts-accent);
707}
708.typeset .ts-notes-marker::before { content: counter(ts-notes-footnote); }
709.typeset { counter-reset: ts-notes-footnote; }
710.typeset .ts-notes-marker { counter-increment: ts-notes-footnote; }
711
712/* True bottom-of-page footnotes need an engine that implements the CSS
713 footnote spec — WeasyPrint 53+ and Prince do; browsers do not. Where they
714 are unavailable this degrades to an endnotes block, which is why the notes
715 live in the document rather than in a generated-content property. */
716@supports (float: footnote) {
717 /* @style letter-footnote — a letter's footnote is the document footnote mechanism: the marker above and the endnotes block below. */
718 .typeset .ts-notes-footnote {
719 float: footnote;
720 footnote-display: block;
721 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
722 line-height: 1.35;
723 }
724 .typeset .ts-notes-endnotes { display: none; }
725}
726
727.typeset .ts-notes-endnotes {
728 text-align: left;
729 margin-top: calc(var(--ts-space) * 2);
730 padding-top: var(--ts-space);
731 border-top: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
732 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
733 line-height: 1.4;
734 counter-reset: ts-endnote;
735}
736.typeset .ts-notes-endnotes ol { padding-left: 1.8em; }
737.typeset .ts-notes-endnotes li { margin-bottom: 0.4em; }
738
739/* Sidenotes: no page-break arithmetic, and the reader never loses their
740 place. They cost you a wide right margin. */
741/* The reserved margin must be wide enough for the gap plus the note: 2em + 11em
742 here, with an em to spare. */
743.typeset--sidenotes { --ts-measure: 27em; padding-right: 14em; }
744.typeset--sidenotes p { position: relative; }
745.typeset .ts-notes-sidenote {
746 position: absolute;
747
748 /* Anchored to the paragraph's own right edge, NOT to `calc(measure + 2em)`.
749 The measure is a max-width, so the paragraph is whichever is narrower —
750 the measure, or what the container's padding leaves it. Offsetting from the
751 measure therefore puts the note in the wrong place whenever the padding is
752 the binding constraint, and it lands on top of the text. */
753 left: 100%;
754 margin-left: 2em;
755 width: 11em;
756 margin-top: -0.3em;
757 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
758 font-size: var(--ts-xs);
759 line-height: 1.4;
760 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
761 text-align: left;
762 text-indent: 0;
763}
764.typeset .ts-notes-sidenote::before {
765 content: counter(ts-notes-footnote) " ";
766 color: var(--ts-accent);
767 font-weight: 600;
768}
769/*! @e */
770
771/*! @s callouts :: Callouts */
772.typeset .ts-callouts-callout {
773 margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.25) 0;
774 padding: 0.75em 1em;
775 border: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
776 border-left: 2.5pt solid var(--ts-rule-strong);
777 background: var(--ts-wash);
778 font-size: 10pt;
779 break-inside: avoid;
780}
781.typeset .ts-callouts-callout > :last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }
782.typeset .ts-callouts-title {
783 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
784 font-size: var(--ts-xs);
785 font-weight: 700;
786 letter-spacing: 0.09em;
787 text-transform: uppercase;
788 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
789 margin-bottom: 0.35em;
790}
791.typeset .ts-callouts-warning { border-left-color: var(--ts-accent); }
792.typeset .ts-callouts-warning .ts-callouts-title { color: var(--ts-accent); }
793/*! @e */
794
795/*! @s breaks :: Section breaks */
796/* A blank line cannot survive a page break — if the break falls on the gap,
797 the reader never sees it. Use a visible mark: one of the four variants
798 below, each supplying its own ::before content.
799
800 This rule is the block geometry a bare <hr> and .ts-break both need —
801 internal, and it renders no mark of its own. The mark comes from the
802 ::before of a specific variant (or, for <hr>, the rule right below). */
803.typeset hr,
804.typeset .ts-break {
805 border: 0;
806 height: auto;
807 margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5) 0;
808 text-align: center;
809 text-align-last: center; /* a one-line block IS its own last line */
810 color: var(--ts-ink-faint);
811 break-after: avoid;
812}
813/* A bare <hr> carries no variant class, so its mark is fixed here: three
814 widely spaced asterisks, the same values .ts-breaks-asterisks::before
815 uses below for a document that spells the choice out explicitly. */
816.typeset hr::before {
817 content: "* * *";
818 letter-spacing: 0.6em;
819 font-size: 10pt;
820}
821
822/* Three widely spaced asterisks, the default treatment. */
823.typeset .ts-breaks-asterisks::before { content: "* * *"; letter-spacing: 0.6em; font-size: 10pt; }
824/* An asterism, for a heavier division. */
825.typeset .ts-breaks-asterism::before { content: "⁂"; letter-spacing: 0; font-size: 14pt; }
826/* A fleuron, for a decorative one. */
827.typeset .ts-breaks-fleuron::before { content: "❦"; letter-spacing: 0; font-size: 12pt; color: var(--ts-accent); }
828/* A plain rule, for a report. */
829.typeset .ts-breaks-rule::before { content: none; }
830.typeset .ts-breaks-rule { border-top: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule); height: 0; }
831/*! @e */
832
833/*! @s frontmatter :: Front matter */
834.typeset .ts-frontmatter-title-block {
835 margin-bottom: calc(var(--ts-space) * 3);
836 padding-bottom: var(--ts-space);
837 border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
838}
839.typeset .ts-frontmatter-title-block h1 { margin-bottom: 0.25em; }
840.typeset .ts-frontmatter-subtitle {
841 text-align: left;
842 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
843 font-size: var(--ts-h3);
844 font-weight: 300;
845 line-height: 1.25;
846 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
847 margin: 0 0 var(--ts-space);
848 text-wrap: balance;
849}
850.typeset .ts-frontmatter-byline {
851 text-align: left;
852 font-variant-caps: all-small-caps;
853 letter-spacing: 0.08em;
854 font-size: var(--ts-base);
855 margin: 0;
856}
857.typeset .ts-frontmatter-dateline {
858 text-align: left;
859 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
860 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
861 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
862 margin: 0.2em 0 0;
863}
864
865.typeset .ts-frontmatter-abstract {
866 text-align: left;
867 font-size: 10pt;
868 line-height: 1.45;
869 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
870 max-width: 30em;
871 margin-bottom: calc(var(--ts-space) * 2);
872}
873.typeset .ts-frontmatter-abstract-label {
874 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
875 font-size: var(--ts-xs);
876 font-weight: 700;
877 font-variant-caps: normal;
878 letter-spacing: 0.1em;
879 text-transform: uppercase;
880 color: var(--ts-ink-faint);
881 display: block;
882 margin-bottom: 0.3em;
883}
884
885/* The colophon closes the document: how it was made, and in what. */
886.typeset .ts-frontmatter-colophon {
887 text-align: left;
888 margin-top: calc(var(--ts-space) * 3);
889 padding-top: var(--ts-space);
890 border-top: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
891 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
892 font-style: italic;
893 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
894 max-width: 26em;
895 break-before: avoid;
896}
897/*! @e */
898
899/*! @s toc :: Table of contents */
900/* Dot leaders and real page numbers need `target-counter()` — a paged-media
901 engine only. In a browser the leaders render and the numbers do not. */
902.typeset .ts-toc { text-align: left; font-family: var(--ts-sans); font-size: var(--ts-sm); }
903.typeset .ts-toc ol { padding-left: 0; }
904/* @style toc-entry */
905.typeset .ts-toc li { margin-bottom: 0.35em; }
906.typeset .ts-toc li::before { content: none; }
907.typeset .ts-toc a {
908 display: flex;
909 align-items: baseline;
910 gap: 0.4em;
911 text-decoration: none;
912}
913.typeset .ts-toc a::after {
914 content: target-counter(attr(href url), page);
915 font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums;
916 color: var(--ts-ink-muted);
917}
918.typeset .ts-toc .ts-toc-leader {
919 flex: 1;
920 border-bottom: 0.5pt dotted var(--ts-rule);
921 transform: translateY(-0.15em);
922}
923.typeset .ts-toc .ts-toc-entry-2 { padding-left: 1.5em; }
924/*! @e */
925
926/*! @s bibliography :: Bibliography */
927/* Hanging indent: the author's surname is the thing being scanned, so it must
928 be the leftmost thing on the entry. */
929.typeset .ts-bibliography-entry {
930 text-align: left;
931 font-size: var(--ts-sm);
932 line-height: 1.4;
933 padding-left: 0;
934 list-style: none;
935}
936.typeset .ts-bibliography-entry li {
937 padding-left: 1.8em;
938 text-indent: -1.8em;
939 margin-bottom: 0.55em;
940 break-inside: avoid;
941}
942.typeset .ts-bibliography-entry li::before { content: none; }
943.typeset .ts-bibliography-entry cite { font-style: italic; }
944/*! @e */
945
946/*! @s letter :: Letter */
947/* @style letter-page — a letter's own page: no running head, no folio, and a
948 deeper top margin than foot or sides so the sender block sits where an
949 envelope window expects it. */
950.typeset--letter { page: ts-letter; }
951@page ts-letter {
952 margin: 32mm 25mm 28mm;
953 @top-center { content: none; }
954 @bottom-center { content: none; }
955}
956
957/* The sender block is address data, not a masthead: one style throughout, at
958 body size, in the reading face. A personal letter does not announce itself —
959 the recipient knows who writes to them. Nothing here is bold, and nothing is
960 set in the sans, so the block recedes and the letter starts sooner. */
961.typeset .ts-letter-sender {
962 text-align: left;
963 font-size: var(--ts-base);
964 line-height: 1.35;
965 color: var(--ts-ink);
966 margin: 0 0 calc(var(--ts-space) * 2.5);
967}
968.typeset .ts-letter-sender p {
969 margin: 0;
970 text-indent: 0;
971}
972
973/* Address blocks are not prose: they are line-broken data. */
974.typeset .ts-letter-address-block {
975 text-align: left;
976 font-style: normal;
977 line-height: 1.35;
978 margin-bottom: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5);
979}
980.typeset .ts-letter-address-label {
981 display: block;
982 font-family: var(--ts-sans);
983 font-size: var(--ts-xs);
984 font-weight: 400;
985 font-variant-caps: normal;
986 letter-spacing: 0.1em;
987 text-transform: uppercase;
988 color: var(--ts-ink-faint);
989 margin-bottom: 0.25em;
990}
991
992.typeset .ts-letter-date {
993 margin-bottom: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5);
994 font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums;
995 text-align: left;
996}
997
998/* A line under the date, in italic — a dedication, a feast, a devotion. It
999 belongs to the date rather than following it, so it climbs back over the
1000 date's gap and carries that gap itself. Written against the same token as the
1001 date's margin so the two cannot drift apart.
1002
1003 Deliberately not `.ts-letter-date:has(+ .ts-letter-date-note)`: Paged.js's
1004 CSS parser does not understand `:has()` any more than it understands `:is()`,
1005 and a selector it cannot parse aborts pagination outright. */
1006.typeset .ts-letter-date-note {
1007 margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * -1.5 + 0.1em) 0 calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5);
1008 font-style: italic;
1009 text-indent: 0;
1010}
1011.typeset .ts-letter-salutation { margin-bottom: var(--ts-space); text-align: left; }
1012.typeset .ts-letter-closing { margin: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5) 0 0; text-align: left; }
1013
1014/* The typed name, with room above it to sign. No rule: a ruled line is a form
1015 to be filled in, and this is a letter. */
1016.typeset .ts-letter-signature {
1017 text-align: left;
1018 margin-top: calc(var(--ts-space) * 3);
1019 text-indent: 0;
1020 break-inside: avoid;
1021}
1022.typeset .ts-letter-signature img { display: block; max-height: 16mm; margin-bottom: 0.2em; }
1023
1024/* Same reasoning as the postscript: "Enc." introduces a sentence, it does not
1025 head a section. Left as the only small-caps label in a letter it was the one
1026 thing on the page shouting. */
1027.typeset .ts-letter-enclosures {
1028 text-align: left;
1029 margin-top: calc(var(--ts-space) * 2);
1030 font-size: var(--ts-base);
1031 text-indent: 0;
1032}
1033/* A postscript is a sentence that happens to begin with "P.S." — the label is
1034 not a heading, so it matches the text it introduces exactly. */
1035.typeset .ts-letter-postscript {
1036 text-align: left;
1037 margin-top: var(--ts-space);
1038 font-size: var(--ts-base);
1039 text-indent: 0;
1040}
1041/*! @e */
1042
1043/*! @s two-column :: Two column, equal */
1044/* Papers, journal articles, newsletters, technical notes — documents scanned
1045 and referenced as much as read.
1046
1047 The base size drops to 9.5pt here, and that is arithmetic rather than taste:
1048 an 82mm column carries 43 characters at 11pt, below the 45-character floor
1049 this stylesheet sets for a line of prose. 9.5pt restores 50. An
1050 implementation that keeps 11pt in two columns breaks the measure rule, which
1051 is the rule everything else is downstream of. */
1052.typeset--two-column {
1053 /* Every step comes down. A 24pt heading in an 82mm column spends three lines
1054 saying two words. */
1055 --ts-xs: 7pt;
1056 --ts-sm: 8.5pt;
1057 --ts-base: 9.5pt;
1058 --ts-h4: 9.5pt;
1059 --ts-h3: 11pt;
1060 --ts-h2: 13pt;
1061 --ts-h1: 20pt;
1062
1063 /* Leading tightens with the measure: a shorter line needs less separation to
1064 keep the return sweep unambiguous. */
1065 --ts-leading: 1.4;
1066 --ts-space: 9.5pt;
1067
1068 /* The column IS the measure, so the character cap comes off. */
1069 --ts-measure: none;
1070 --ts-column-gap: 6mm;
1071
1072 /* A blank line costs 3% of a column, so paragraphs indent here by default —
1073 not as an option. */
1074 --ts-para-gap: 0;
1075 --ts-para-indent: 1.25em;
1076
1077 font-size: var(--ts-base);
1078 columns: 2;
1079 column-gap: var(--ts-column-gap);
1080 column-fill: balance; /* the final page balances its columns */
1081
1082 /* Justification with hyphenation is MANDATORY at this measure, not optional:
1083 at 50 characters a ragged edge serrates the column and the word gaps read
1084 as rivers. This is the one place the stylesheet removes a choice. */
1085 text-align: justify;
1086 text-align-last: left;
1087 hyphens: auto;
1088 hyphenate-limit-chars: 6 3 3;
1089 hyphenate-limit-lines: 2;
1090}
1091
1092/* Spans both columns, always — templates.two-column.spanning.always in
1093 spec.json, unmarked. Each is a direct child of the multicol container,
1094 which is what column-span requires. */
1095.typeset--two-column > .ts-frontmatter-title-block,
1096.typeset--two-column > .ts-frontmatter-subtitle,
1097.typeset--two-column > .ts-frontmatter-byline,
1098.typeset--two-column > .ts-frontmatter-dateline,
1099.typeset--two-column > .ts-frontmatter-abstract,
1100.typeset--two-column > h1,
1101.typeset--two-column > .ts-frontmatter-colophon,
1102.typeset--two-column > .ts-span {
1103 column-span: all;
1104}
1105
1106/* Spanning is opt-in per instance for figures and tables: it costs a break in
1107 both columns, so the default stays column-width. A spanning element must sit
1108 at the top or the bottom of the page, never mid-column. */
1109.typeset--two-column > .ts-span {
1110 break-before: avoid-column;
1111 margin-bottom: calc(var(--ts-space) * 1.5);
1112}
1113
1114/* An optional hairline where the columns need separating. Most journals omit
1115 it — the gutter is already doing the work. */
1116.typeset--two-column.typeset--column-rule {
1117 column-rule: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
1118}
1119
1120/* A sidenote has no margin to live in here. Rather than let it be positioned
1121 off the page and silently lost, it degrades to an inline aside. */
1122.typeset--two-column .ts-notes-sidenote {
1123 position: static;
1124 display: block;
1125 width: auto;
1126 margin: 0.4em 0;
1127 padding-left: 0.6em;
1128 border-left: 0.5pt solid var(--ts-rule);
1129 text-indent: 0;
1130}
1131
1132/* A three-line cap at 3.05em is 29pt — 10mm of the column given to one
1133 letter. The opening small caps carry the signal instead. */
1134.typeset--two-column .ts-dropcap::first-letter {
1135 float: none;
1136 font-size: inherit;
1137 line-height: inherit;
1138 color: inherit;
1139 padding: 0;
1140}
1141
1142/* Denser matter for a narrower column. */
1143.typeset--two-column blockquote { font-size: 9pt; padding-left: var(--ts-space); }
1144.typeset--two-column table { font-size: 8pt; line-height: 1.3; }
1145.typeset--two-column pre { font-size: 7.5pt; }
1146.typeset--two-column figcaption { font-size: 8pt; }
1147.typeset--two-column .ts-notes-endnotes { font-size: 8.5pt; }
1148.typeset--two-column .ts-quotes-pullquote { font-size: 12pt; }
1149.typeset--two-column .ts-frontmatter-abstract { font-size: 9pt; max-width: none; }
1150.typeset--two-column .ts-quotes-epigraph { max-width: none; }
1151/*! @e */
1152
1153/*! @s utilities :: Pagination utilities */
1154.ts-utilities-break-before { break-before: page; }
1155.ts-utilities-break-after { break-after: page; }
1156.ts-utilities-keep-together { break-inside: avoid; page-break-inside: avoid; }
1157.ts-utilities-no-hyphens { hyphens: manual; }
1158
1159/* Non-breaking spaces belong in the markup, but these catch the common cases:
1160 a figure and its unit, an initial and a surname. */
1161.ts-utilities-tie { white-space: nowrap; }
1162
1163/* @style utilities-print-only — names the pair: this block and the .ts-print-only block right below it. */
1164@media print {
1165 .ts-screen-only { display: none !important; }
1166}
1167@media screen {
1168 .ts-print-only { display: none !important; }
1169}
1170
1171/* Force backgrounds and rules to survive the print dialog's ink-saving. */
1172/* @style utilities-color-adjust */
1173@media print {
1174 .typeset,
1175 .typeset * {
1176 -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact;
1177 print-color-adjust: exact;
1178 }
1179}
1180/*! @e */
